issues.description: The problem statement requires a Book struct with properties named `title`, `author`, and an optional `genres`. In the solution, the Book struct declares `let bookTitle: String` (instead of `title`), while Client code in the solution refers to `book.title` and also constructs Books with `Book(title: ..., author: ..., genres: ...)`. This name mismatch between the Book definition and its use will cause compile errors and confuses students about the expected property names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Book struct match the problem specification and the way it's used in Client: rename `bookTitle` to `title` (so the synthesized initializer and property accessors are `title`, `author`, `genres`), or alternatively, update all uses and initializer calls to use `bookTitle` consistently. The preferred fix is to rename the struct property to `title` to align with the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement defines a Book struct with a String field named `title`, and the Client implementation expects `book.title`. However the solution's Book struct declares this property as `bookTitle`. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual field (book title) creates a mapping confusion and will cause compilation mismatch between the Book definition and its use.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the Book struct property `bookTitle` to `title` in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so it matches the problem statement and the Client usage (book.title). Alternatively, update all references (including the problem statement and Client) to consistently use `bookTitle`, but using `title` is recommended for clarity and to match the specification.
